They compete in the {{English football updater|StokeCty}}, the second tier of [[English football league system|English football]]. Founded as Stoke Ramblers in 1863, the club changed its name to Stoke in 1878 and then to Stoke City in 1925 after Stoke-on-Trent was granted [[City status in the United Kingdom|city status]]. Stoke's home ground is the 30,089 capacity [[bet365 Stadium]]. Before it was opened in 1997, the club was based at the [[Victoria Ground]], which was their home ground since 1878. The club's nickname is The Potters, after the [[Staffordshire Potteries|pottery industry in Stoke-on-Trent]], and their traditional home kit is a red-and-white vertically striped shirt, white shorts and stockings. Their traditional rivals are Midlands clubs [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] and [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]], whilst their local rivals are [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] with whom they contest the [[Potteries derby]]. Stoke were one of the twelve founding members of the [[English Football League|Football League]] in [[1888–89 Football League|1888]]. They failed [[Re-election (Football League)|re-election]] in 1890, but were re-admitted after winning the [[1890–91 Stoke F.C. season|1890–91]] [[Football Alliance]] title. The club were relegated from the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] in 1907 and entered liquidation the following year. Though the club was saved, they were not re-elected until 1915, and instead spent the intervening years in the [[West Midlands (Regional) League|Birmingham & District League]] and [[Southern Football League|Southern League]]. Promoted from the [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]] in [[1921–22 Football League|1921–22]], the club were relegated twice in four years by 1926. Stoke won the [[Football League Third Division North|Third Division North]] in [[1926–27 Stoke City F.C. season|1926–27]] and then the Second Division title in [[1932–33 Football League|1932–33]]. They remained in the top-flight for twenty years and then spent a decade in the Second Division, before winning promotion as champions in [[1962–63 Football League|1962–63]]. Under the stewardship of [[Tony Waddington]], Stoke won the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] in [[1972 Football League Cup final|1972]] with a 2–1 victory over [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Stoke had also been beaten finalists in [[1964 Football League Cup final|1964]]. The club spent fourteen years in the top-flight, and would secure promotion in [[1978–79 Football League|1978–79]] after being relegated two years earlier. Stoke remained in the top-flight from 1979 to 1985, though were relegated to the [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]] in 1990. Having won the [[EFL Trophy|Football League Trophy]] in [[1992 Associate Members' Cup final|1992]], they were promoted as champions in [[1992–93 Football League|1992–93]]. Relegation in 1998 allowed the club to win another Football League Trophy title in [[2000 Football League Trophy final|2000]], before promotion was secured with victory in the [[2002 Football League Second Division play-off final|2002 play-off final]]. Manager [[Tony Pulis]] took Stoke into the [[Premier League]] at the end of the [[2007–08 Football League Championship|2007–08 campaign]]. They played in the [[FA Cup final|final]] of the [[FA Cup]] in [[2011 FA Cup final|2011]], finishing runners-up to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], which saw the club qualify for [[Stoke City F.C. in European football|European football]]. Ten years of Premier League football culminated in relegation to the EFL Championship in 2018."}}
